{"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-9098.1","title":"Chaos latency tests skip bounds when count==0","description":"CORRECTNESS review of python/tests/sim/test_multihop_latency_bounds.py (min-delivery asserts). Distinct from nvod (concurrent TX) and ffrp (bursty traffic).

test_latency_bounded_with_added_delay (line 319) and test_latency_bounded_with_degraded_signal (line 355) still wrap the only latency-bound checks in:

    if stats.count > 0 and stats.max_us is not None:
        assert stats.max_us <= ...

When stats.count == 0 the tests pass without verifying any bound. Contrast test_three_node_line (line 122) which asserts MIN_DELIVERIES_FOR_STATS, and the nvod/ffrp fixes which converted the same if-guards into asserts.

Worse for the delay test: LatencyRule eligibility in radio.py drops candidates until current_time_us >= transmission.end_time_us + added_latency_us. The test polls get_rx_result("relay") at TX-start (line 308) then advances 400ms without re-polling. With added_us=50_000 the candidate is ineligible at poll time, result is None, no relay runs, count stays 0. The if-guard makes this test a permanent no-op.

Fix: assert a minimum delivery count (MIN_DELIVERIES_FOR_STATS, or at least 1), and for LatencyRule poll after TX-end + added_us has elapsed.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"me@mark.atwood.name","created_at":"2026-08-24T05:08:43.817974Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-08-24T05:08:43.817974Z","labels":["correctness","review","ultracode"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-9098.1","depends_on_id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-9098","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-08-24T05:08:44.313352Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","metadata":"{}"},{"issue_id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-9098.1","depends_on_id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-nvod","type":"discovered-from","created_at":"2026-08-24T05:08:44.706702Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","metadata":"{}"}]}
